chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: Two sealed measures of barley are not to be sold for one sealed measure of wheat, and they are not to be sold except like for like, and the same applies to dates.

He said: And he was asked about a man who buys wheat and finds with its owner only barley, is it permissible for him to take two for one? He said: No, for the origin of both is one, and Ali (peace be upon him) used to count barley as equal to wheat.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling barley for wheat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'mithlan bi-mithl' (equal for equal) in the sale of specific foodstuffs, emphasizing that wheat, barley, and dates are treated as a single category of origin. It clarifies that the prohibition against unequal ratios (e.g., two barley for one wheat) stems from their shared nature, a ruling attributed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and rooted in the practice of Imam Ali (AS). This establishes a foundational legal precedent for commodity exchange in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring fairness and preventing hidden interest (riba) in barter transactions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin usman, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Do not sell two sealed container of barley with one sealed container of wheat, and do not buy except similar with similar; and the dates are similar to that’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And he<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the man who bought the wheat, so he could not find with his companions except for barley, is it correct for him that he takes two by one?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No. But rather, the origin of both of them is one, and Ali<sup>asws</sup> used to count the barley with the wheat (as equal)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is not permissible to sell two Makhtum (a container) of barley for one Makhtum of wheat. These items cannot be exchanged except in equal quantities of each other and so also is the date.’

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the case of a man who buys wheat but cannot find with his party anything except barley, if he can take two for one. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, because the origin of the two is the same and Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would count barley for wheat.’”
